## Keys changed: Ctrl and Alt mean what they mean in ZTreeWin

**Ctrl+letter** acts on the tagged files, as before. **Alt+letter** no longer
repeats it: it is the other version of a command, as in ZTreeWin. In the tree
it acts on the whole branch, in the file window on the tagged files with their
paths, and it holds the tools.

| Key | Up to 0.7 | From 0.8 |
|---|---|---|
| Alt+A | Attributes of the tagged files | nothing (use Ctrl+A) |
| Alt+D | delete the tagged files | **Duplicates** (deleting them: Ctrl+D) |
| Alt+R | rename the tagged files | **Release** the branch, as `-` (renaming them: Ctrl+R) |
| Alt+T | tag everything | nothing (use Ctrl+T) |
| Alt+U | untag everything | **Usage** (untagging: Ctrl+U) |
| Alt+W | Usage | nothing (use Alt+U) |
| Alt+Y | Duplicates | nothing (use Alt+D) |

If you used Alt+D to delete the tagged files, it now opens Duplicates, which
deletes nothing without asking. The old keys can be brought back in
`[keys.any]` of `config.toml`, for instance `"alt+w" = "usage"`.

The ALT menu follows: in alphabetical order, as the other menus, and each word
has its own letter. Alt+X (the terminal) and Alt+O (type the tagged files in
it) are on its second line; Alt+Z, full screen, in the terminal's own menu.
See "What Ctrl and Alt mean" in the manual's tagging page.

## A footer of three lines: no hidden commands

Every command now has its place in a menu. The footer has three lines on an
ordinary screen: the letter commands in alphabetical order on the first two,
the function keys and symbols on the third. On a screen wide enough for every
menu, it has two, and the tree keeps that line. What used to work without showing is now there: **N**ew
date (Ctrl+N for the tagged files), **A**vailable, `?` statistics, `\`
Treespec, F5 and Ctrl+F5 archive, F7 Autoview, F12 setup, Ctrl+B Batch,
Ctrl+S Search and Ctrl+V View of the tagged files, Ctrl+F7/F8/F9 on the
branch, Alt+Q Quit here. Inside an archive or on a remote machine the menus
leave out what does not work there (the REMOTE menu now shows what 0.7 can do
on another machine).

## Menus that do not fit

A footer menu too wide for the window shortens its words, all to the same
length and never losing the highlighted letter, before it leaves any out; what
still does not fit goes from the end, with a `…` in its place, and F9 (or Esc)
always stays.

## Tables with no limit of 50,000 rows

With **V**, a CSV or TSV file, JSON Lines, a dBase file (`.dbf`), and a table,
view or query of a SQLite database show all their rows, however many. The
grid keeps the rows near the cursor and reads the others as you move, with the
screen always free: a row not read yet shows as `…` for a moment.

- **The total** shows while it is counted, `2,000+ (counting…)`, and then the
  real number. **Ctrl+End** goes to the last row and `g` to any.
- **The filter** (`&`) goes over the whole table, in the background, saying how
  far it got; the matches show as they are found, up to 1,000,000.
- **Esc** stops the count or the filter, keeping what they found so far.
- **When the file changes** while it is open, Xylem stops reading it and says
  so: **R** reads it again.
- **A big table opens at once:** its text and hex are read only when you go to
  them (T, H). A 330 MB database that took seconds now opens right away.

Spreadsheets (XLSX, XLSB, XLS, ODS) cannot be read in parts and keep the limit
of 50,000 rows; past it, the header says so and **O** opens the sheet in your
spreadsheet program. Autoview (F7) still reads only the first rows. Parquet
comes in a later version.

## Small things

- **Seconds in the clock:** F12, page 2, **Q** (or `clock_seconds = true`).
  Off by default; on, the clock ticks right after each second turns.
- **B in Branch or Showall** goes back to the directory's own list, instead of
  building the same Branch again.
- **The small file window** under the tree takes a quarter of the height: more
  files on a tall terminal, the tree keeping the most of a short one (at least
  3 files). On an ordinary 34-row screen it is the same as before.
